FILED s519a (Opus 5.5, 2026-10-18), found reading Path-Tiny t/filesystem.t row 17 (`1 while unlink $file; ok not -e $file;`) after #3374 let the file run.  SILENT WRONG.

REPRODUCER (scratch/s519a/pr/pt6.pl): use Path::Tiny; my $file = path("/tmp/x.txt"); (create it); my $n = 0; $n++ while unlink $file; print "n=$n exists=", (-e $file ? 1 : 0)
perl 5.40.3: `n=1 exists=0`.  PCL: `n=0 exists=1`.
CAUSE: cl/pcl-runtime.lisp p-unlink passes `(to-string (unbox f))` to unlink(2); to-string does not run a `""` overload, so the path is "Path::Tiny=ARRAY(0x...)".  The filetests go through %p-stat-operand, which does.  Check the other filename-taking builtins (rename, chmod, chown, utime, mkdir, rmdir, opendir, open with a 3-arg path) for the same shortcut -- the #119/#402 family (stringify instead of overload); ONE overload-aware path coercion for all of them (rule 11).

=== DONE (s520a, Opus 5.5, 2026-10-18) ===
Commit 51337656.  ONE coercion `%p-path-string` (to-string of the operand AS IT ARRIVED, the box not peeled, so a `""` overload / tie FETCH runs -- the filetests' #1031 rule) for stat/lstat, open's path, unlink, chmod, chown, utime, rename, link, symlink, readlink, mkdir, rmdir, truncate; a BLESSED scalar ref is a path to open, never an in-memory target (a plain \$s still is one).  Probes p2/*.pl = perl (overloaded object, plain string, handle where perl takes one).  Guard Pl/t/overload-01.t row 48 (inverse FAILS on fd04c048).  Acceptance: Path-Tiny t/filesystem.t row 17 (`1 while unlink $file`) passes in the one-file run; its row left cpan-board14-fails.tsv by edit (b4200d31).  ir-spec §3.2.  Batch bars: session-log ## Session s520a.
subject: `unlink $obj` with a `""`-overloaded object (a Path::Tiny path) deletes nothing and answers 0: p-unlink stringifies with to-string, which skips the overload (-e on the same object is right)
